newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Pripps-Ringes says talks with Coca-Cola in trouble.
newsitem.headline: Pripps-Ringes says talks with Coca-Cola in trouble.

text.p: Nordic drinks group Pripps-Ringnes on Monday said negotiations with Coca-Cola over winding up a production and distribution alliance in Sweden and Norway had hit difficulties but talks were continuing.
"We are still in negotiations. It might be difficult to reach the terms we came to in June," Paul Bergqvist from Pripps Ringnes told Reuters.
Last year Coca-Cola cancelled a 43-year-old licensing deal with Pripps Ringnes, a joint venture of Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo and Norwegian conglomerate Orkla ASA .
The reason for the fall-out was not known but some market players suggested Coca-Cola was unhappy with its Swedish sales.
But in June this year the two companies entered into a letter of intent concerning the winding up of their cooperation in Norway and Sweden.
They decided to proceed with distribution uninterrupted until February 1997 in Sweden and Norway.
Pripps Ringnes was to continue to produce Coca-Cola in these markets until the end of 1998.
The parties subsequently agreed to extend cooperation on sales and distribution in Norway until May 1, 1997.
"It now appears clear that the parties will not reach agreement on finalising the negotiations on the basis of the letter of intent," Pripps Ringnes said in a statement.
"However negotiations on adequate agreements concerning the winding up of cooperation in Norway and Sweden are continuing."
Coca-Cola has been in talks with Denmark's Carlsberg over future production and marketing in Sweden and Norway.
Carlsberg has such an agreement with Coca-Cola in Denmark.
Pripps Ringnes said it was negotiating with a view to finalising the deal as soon as possible.
But it said it it was impossible to reach an agreement the cooperation between the parties would be based on the agreements that existed before the above-mentioned letter of intent was entered into.
This mean in Sweden the contract will end on April 1, 1997 and from that date Coca-Cola will take responsibility for its own production and distribution.

"Pripps has previously stated that the company disputes Coca-Cola's legal right to cancel the agreement in Sweden and Pripps will as a consequence of a cancellation bring a claim for compensation against Coca-Cola," the company said.
In Norway Pripps Ringnes will continue to bottle, distribute and sell Cocal-Cola products until December 31, 1999.
